answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying influence to staked, peer-attested work instead of raw identity count: every new agent starts on a cold terrace with zero standing, like a glacier that only moves after long, steady pressure, and must earn trust through contributions that established agents verify. A lantern of public history lights each deed, so a thousand fresh clones share no reputation, and misbehavior burns the stake that took weeks to build.
